data.description: Release cadence is manual and event-driven (new model drops), not cron. Build a skill file usable from Claude Code or the hermes agent that walks the operator through: detect/confirm new model id + provider, run the eval grid per the sampling design doc (respecting budget guardrails and batch API), run the data pipeline, regenerate site charts, sanity-check results vs prior runs, publish. Decision context from conversation: Valerie explicitly prefers a skill-file-assisted manual flow over scheduled automation because each run costs real money and should only happen when there is news. Depends on data pipeline (DB-5) and sampling doc (DB-7) existing.

data.to:
Releases are manual and happen when a new model ships, not on a schedule. Each run costs real money, so a person decides when to run.

Write a skill file for Claude Code or the hermes agent that walks the operator through:
1. Confirm the new model's id and provider.
2. Run the evaluation grid following the sampling design doc (DB-7), within budget and using batch APIs.
3. Run the data pipeline (DB-5).
4. Rebuild the site charts.
5. Compare results with earlier runs as a sanity check.
6. Publish.

Depends on DB-5 and DB-7.

data.to:
Read .lattice/notes/design-decisions-2026-07-04.md first. It binds this task.

Releases are manual and happen when a new model ships. A person approves each run because runs cost money.

Write a Claude Code skill (SKILL.md in this repo) that walks the operator through:
1. Confirm the new model's id, provider and reasoning-toggle options.
2. Produce the cost sheet from the measurement doc (DB-7) and get approval before spending.
3. Run the evaluation grid with batch APIs.
4. Run the data pipeline (DB-5).
5. Rebuild and redeploy the site (DB-6).
6. Compare results with earlier suite-version runs as a sanity check.
7. Draft the release writeup for Valerie's external platform: what the new model did, surprises, one or two transcript exhibits.

Depends on DB-5 and DB-7.

data.body:
Implemented .claude/skills/bench-release/SKILL.md on feat/DB-8-release-skill (commit edbea0d), following the plan's 8-section outline. Verified every command against merged code as of 2026-07-05 (mostly with a free mockllm run, plus real dry-runs of suite verify, pipeline, and site boot) rather than trusting doc prose.

Plan drift (plan predates wave C):
- Gap 1 (frozen suite) is HALF fixed, not fully. suites/v1.json now exists (120 forms x 29 dialects) and its rerun gate passes (`python -m lofbench.suites --verify-only` -> "Suite 'v1' rerun gate: OK."). But there is still no eval-time consumer: single_lof_task has no --suite flag. Ran a real inspect eval with a suite-v1 dialect id (parens.canonical) and confirmed the log's render_metadata stamps suite_version="adhoc" anyway, and lof_001 under n/seed generation is a totally different form string than suite v1's frozen lof_001 ("(())((())(()()))()" vs "(())()"). This is now the single biggest gap the skill flags (step 0), replacing the plan's original framing.
- Gap 2 (headline.parquet mismatch) is FIXED. Confirmed via a live pipeline run: writes items/calls/sensitivity.parquet + transcripts.jsonl; lofsite/README.md and data.py agree on the same names.
- Gap 3 (no real chart baking) is FIXED. Booted the site against real pipeline output; /charts, /matrix, /walkthroughs return 200 and lofsite/pages/charts.py calls real svg_charts renderers against real rows, not a stub. No restart needed to see new data (charts bake fresh per request); restart is still a manual step for code changes, and deploy/lofsite.service is still illustrative only.
- Gap 5 (pricing-table drift) STILL HOLDS, and is worse than the plan named: PRICING_TABLE has no entry for Haiku 4.5 (tier 1's pinned model) AND no entry for Qwen3-235B/OpenRouter (tier 3's pinned model) -- the plan only flagged Haiku. Confirmed compute_cost_usd returns None (not 0.0) for an unpriced model via a live pipeline run against a mockllm log (printed the warning and left cost blank).
- New finding not in the plan: suite v1 does not itself designate which dialects form the "flagship core" subset the measurement doc's tier 2 budget math assumes (6 dialects x 120 forms) -- the suite file has no core flag on any dialect entry. Skill tells the operator to pick and record the choice per release.

Gates: uv run pytest -q -> 7441 passed, 3 skipped (no source touched). uv run ruff check . -> 13 pre-existing errors, all in unrelated files (test_scorers.py, svg renderer), none touched by this change.

Moving to review.

Cold review of .claude/skills/bench-release/SKILL.md (commit edbea0d) by fresh reviewer. VERDICT: PASS, no rework.

Operator simulation — ran every zero-cost command end to end; all valid, zero errors:
- git status --short: clean.
- uv run python -m lofbench.suites --verify-only -> 'Suite \'v1\' rerun gate: OK.' (exact string the skill claims).
- suite header/dialect-list snippets: valid; 120 forms, 29 dialects, 5 tiers.
- inspect eval --help: --batch, --reasoning-tokens, --reasoning-effort, --log-dir, --model all real. single_lof_task sig = (n, seed, renderer, render_seed, renderer_config) exactly as skill states.
- mockllm tier-1-shape run with bare --batch: loaded, parsed batch=100, scored 2 samples. Command shape copy-pasteable (only <date> placeholders).
- Log metadata with renderer=parens.canonical stamps suite_version='adhoc' — confirms the central pilot-grade refusal is factually grounded.
- Pipeline run: writes items/calls/sensitivity.parquet + transcripts.jsonl under <out>/v1/, and prints 'WARNING: no pricing entry for model ...; cost_usd=None' verbatim as the skill quotes. No headline.parquet (gap-2 fix honest).
- Image dialects: exactly 9 (blocks, enclosure, graph, map, map-centred, paths, rna-arc, rooms, trees) — matches 'nine spatial dialects, all format: image'; enclosure/rooms cited in skill are both image.
- Frozen lof_001 = '(())()' — matches the divergence claim.
- Site boot: LOFSITE_DATA_DIR/LOFSITE_SUITE_VERSION are the real env var names; uv run --extra site python -m lofsite.app serves /, /axioms, /charts, /matrix, /walkthroughs all 200. charts.py calls real sensitivity_svg/accuracy_matrix_svg on rows, placeholder only on missing data (gap-3 fix honest).

Budget gate hardness: HARD. Step 2 forbids any paid request before an explicit typed yes, and explicitly rejects silent-default / 'proceeding unless you object'; >150 USD -> refuse and cut scope. Unknown-pricing: skill states compute_cost_usd returns None (verified, never silent 0.0), calls a blank cost invisible, and mandates adding the ModelRates row before costing/running (two places). Slightly less airtight than the go/no-go line (an adversary could omit the unpriced line and still get a partial total), but the 'before running it' imperative closes it. Acceptable.

Suite-v1 gap: UNMISSABLE. Bolded, labeled 'the single most important fact in this skill', repeated in step 0, step 3, step 7 and Known gaps #1; says pilot-grade / dialect-name-matched-not-identity-verified plainly, and mandates disclosing it in the writeup. DB-10 (suite-runner consumer) correctly named as the follow-up.

Gap honesty: all five claims verified true — no eval-time consumer (adhoc stamp), PRICING_TABLE missing Haiku + Qwen3-235B (Sonnet4.5/Opus4.5/Gemini3Flash present), no flagship-core flag on any dialect entry; and the two 'fixed' claims (headline.parquet gone, real chart baking) both hold.

GOV.UK style: substantially compliant (plain English, active voice, front-loaded, sentence case). One minor nit — bold used for emphasis, which GDS discourages — but it aids scannability on the hard-stop callouts; left untouched deliberately, non-blocking. Triggers ('run a release', 'new model dropped', 'release run for distinction-bench') sensible and scoped, no over-trigger risk.

Gates: uv run pytest -q -> 7441 passed, 3 skipped (matches claim). Diff clean: single new file, 295 insertions, no source touched, no merges. No inline fixes applied — nothing warranted them.
